APPROVAL RECORD (v1 -> v2): ContactPhone and ContactEmail were approved for automatic backfill. Rationale, from report section 6e: presence is year-correlated rather than random (100% in 2018-2019, 0% phone from 2025), so eligible records cluster in long-closed procurements; the reference holds only 2 distinct phone values and 4 email values. Expected effect on the analysed run: 171 ContactPhone and 242 ContactEmail values recovered, 413 total. CAVEAT THAT DID NOT CHANGE: cross-run volatility for these fields is still unmeasurable from the analysed pair (zero comparable pairs, section 6a), so this approval rests on the static-organisational-data argument, not on measured stability. Backfill copies the matched reference record's own value, never a modal value -- the single purchasing@cob.org record must not be rewritten to bids@cob.org.

APPROVAL RECORD (v2 -> v3): BidType was approved for automatic backfill. Rationale from report section 6: it is a closed five-value taxonomy in the reference (Invitation for Bid/Request a Quote 231, RFP 121, RFQ 114, SOQ 29, Sale of Surplus Property 1), and a solicitation's type is set when it is issued. 495 of 499 matched records are eligible; the other 4 held no BidType in the reference either. BidType is NOT a rule 6 field. CAVEAT: as with the contact fields, cross-run volatility is unmeasurable from the analysed pair -- the candidate holds no BidType values at all, so there are zero comparable pairs. The residual risk is a re-scoped solicitation whose type genuinely changed between runs (an IFB reissued as an RFP, say); that would be silently reinstated as the old type. Nothing in the analysed data shows such a change, and nothing in the analysed data could.

APPROVAL RECORD (v3 -> v4): Title was approved for automatic backfill, 499 eligible records. Title is NOT a rule 6 field. This approval was made with the analysis advising against it, and the reasoning is recorded here so the decision is auditable rather than implicit. AGAINST: unlike BidType, Title is free text rather than a closed taxonomy, so there is no structural reason it cannot change; and as with every other approved field, cross-run volatility is unmeasurable from the analysed pair because the candidate holds no Title values at all. The specific failure mode is a retitled or amended solicitation silently reinstated under its old title -- and because 28 title groups already repeat across the reference (466 distinct titles over 500 records), a stale title reads as entirely plausible to someone reviewing the output. FOR: a title is descriptive of a procurement that has already been issued, 488 of 500 reference records are Awarded and therefore closed, and Title is used in no key -- primaryKey, fallbackKeys, and dedupeKey are all asserted never to reference it -- so a wrong Title cannot corrupt record identity, matching, or deduplication. Every backfilled value is recorded as reference_backfill in the provenance log and is reversible from it.

SCOPE: this profile describes matching, dedupe, and review policy only. It authorizes no writes, no exports, and no external actions. The primary remedy for this regression is a fixed scraper re-run; recovery is a stopgap that must produce a new, clearly-labelled artifact per AGENTS.md rule 2.

CORROBORATION (v4 -> v5): textFields/deadlineCues configure the advisory review signal in src/engine/corroboration.ts. It reads the candidate's surviving Description for a deadline date and compares it with the reference value a backfill would write. MEASURED on the shipped pair: of 499 DueDate backfill candidates, 188 are corroborated by the text, 23 disagree, 288 say nothing -- 89% agreement where the text states a deadline at all, which is what earns DueDate the signal. PublishedDate and AwardDate agree about 2% of the time (the prose is not about them), so the calibration withholds the signal there rather than flagging 44% of records for nothing. The cue list is what separates a submission deadline from a pre-bid walkthrough or a work-completion date; without it, records 60B-2019 and 63B-2023 were flagged wrongly. This signal is advisory under AGENTS.md rule 5: it ranks review candidates and never modifies output, changes a lane, or decides anything. Bumping the version because provenance must identify the policy a decision was made under, and this changes what a reviewer is shown.

VALIDATION (v6 -> v7): the 'validation' block activates the QA engine's configured format checks (src/engine/qa.ts) for this source. Field choices are evidence-backed from the shipped fixture pair (1000 records): BidURL and ResourceURL are absolute https URLs in 1000/1000 records; the six document/hash fields are JSON-encoded strings ('[]' or JSON arrays) in 1000/1000; ContactEmail (bids@cob.org et al) and ContactPhone ((360) 778-7750 et al) are heuristic kinds reported at low severity per the engine's design; DueDate/PublishedDate/AwardDate parse with Date.parse in every populated record ('8/4/2026 11:00 AM', '2/24/2021'). All 13 fields were verified against both fixtures with zero validation failures, so this block cannot manufacture findings on known-good data. Validation REPORTS only (field_validation_failure findings) — it never backfills, never changes a lane, and leaves rule 6 untouched; Created/Refreshed are deliberately omitted because they are excludedFields whose conflicts are already suppressed as per-run stamps. Bumping the version because findings are stamped with profileVersion and a run that starts emitting validation findings is a different policy than one that cannot.
